title: Introducing The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups of 2026
summary: The Information released its annual list of 50 promising early-stage startups, selected on revenue, business models and growth prospects, and for the first time added a dedicated security category. Three of the four most highly valued companies on the list are security startups worth more than $1 billion, and named picks include AI penetration-testing firm Tenzai, Nir Zuk's newly founded Cylake and Noitom Robotics. The publication notes past picks such as Cursor's maker, chosen at a $400 million valuation and later acquired by SpaceX for $60 billion.

title: Jensen Huang's Downfall
summary: WSJ Technology's weekly lead recaps Jensen Huang's rapid exit from Nvidia: within a week he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of passing information to Chinese intelligence, a second affair with a longtime Nvidia executive triggered an emergency board meeting, and he resigned with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. The piece adds WSJ reporting that in his final months Huang clashed with Kress over Nvidia's use of its balance sheet to support cloud startups and backstop data-center projects, warning that an "avalanche" of purchase commitments threatened the company. Investors will hear from Kress when Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.

title: What It Takes to Deliver Your Wings Order During a Football Game, Fast and Hot
summary: The Wall Street Journal looks at how Wingstop relies on its digital ordering infrastructure, with a single order potentially drawing on about 40 different Amazon Web Services cloud services. Nearly 74% of the chain's third-quarter restaurant sales came through its app and online delivery and pickup channels, making fast, reliable technology central to its business during demand spikes such as football games.

title: How Jensen Huang Built the Backdoor Route That Keeps Beijing in the AI Race
summary: The Wall Street Journal examines how large data centers in Southeast Asia, built with Nvidia's cooperation under Jensen Huang, supplied crucial computing power to Chinese companies despite U.S. export controls. The report says these facilities also served as cover for alleged smuggling of restricted chips, adding a national-security dimension to the scandal surrounding Huang's departure.

title: Nvidia CEO Ouster Reverberates Globally
summary: Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO is rippling through the chip sector, AI startups and U.S.-China relations, as workarounds that let Chinese buyers access Nvidia chips may now close and the company's role as a funder of smaller AI firms shrinks. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the board to pick an outside CEO, while the FT reported Huang has privately discussed a return and the board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas. Interim CEO Colette Kress faces her first earnings call on Tuesday after the stock fell 13% last week.

title: The Investors Set to Win Big in Anthropic's IPO
summary: Anthropic's IPO this week is expected to value the Claude developer at $1.33 trillion or more, setting up large payouts for its more than 300 investors, from early angels in its 2021 Series A at a $461 million valuation to backers of its $965 billion Series H in May. The Information expects strong demand to push pricing above the $70–$78 preliminary range and a first-day open potentially well above $100 a share.

title: Nvidia's Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered
summary: Nvidia's role as a major investor in AI startups and cloud partners is expected to shrink under interim CEO Colette Kress, after Huang had already told cloud partners they would need upfront customer payments to get GPUs. UBS estimates the pullback could remove $50 billion or more from the market, with pending deals involving Reflection AI and a planned investment in Thinking Machines Lab at a $40 billion valuation in doubt.

title: Trump Administration to Name Nvidia Among AI 'National Champions'
summary: The Trump administration plans to designate more than two dozen companies, including Nvidia, as AI 'national champions' to spread U.S. AI technology abroad. The designation brings faster export-license approvals, federal financing and government support overseas, and is proceeding despite investigations surrounding Nvidia's China sales.

title: California AG Accuses OpenAI of Misleading and Endangering the Public
summary: California's attorney general has sued OpenAI, alleging the company knowingly developed AI models without necessary safeguards and misled the public. The case is a significant state-level legal challenge to the ChatGPT maker.

title: Big Tech Needs to Spread Its Bets on Data Centers
summary: A Heard on the Street column argues that AI companies concentrating spending on a small number of mega data-center projects look exposed after the midterm elections. It makes the case for diversifying data-center bets to reduce political and execution risk.

title: Thomson Reuters CEO Says Content Is King When It Comes to AI
summary: Thomson Reuters CEO Steve Hasker says the company's proprietary content is its key advantage in AI and that it will keep investing heavily in AI-driven products. The interview reflects how information providers are positioning owned data as a moat against general-purpose AI models.

title: Verizon Trades Network Claims for Pop-Culture Buzz
summary: Under CMO Leslie Berland, who joined in 2024, Verizon has moved away from network-reliability messaging toward pop-culture-driven ads featuring TV heartthrobs, and is building an in-house team to produce ads faster. One spot was pulled after alienating viewers 55 and older, and some observers doubt buzzy ads will get customers to switch carriers.

title: Gucci Is Cutting Prices; Louis Vuitton Is Reluctant to Follow the Trend
summary: Luxury executives are openly debating price cuts to escape a three-year slump as mid-tier luxury growth has evaporated, with LVMH's CFO acknowledging internal discussions while still opposing cuts at Louis Vuitton. Gucci has already reduced prices on some items, including a bag that fell 30% from €3,500 to €2,450 in France since July.

title: Microsoft Data Shows Claude Is Stalling Against Copilot in Office
summary: Internal Microsoft data reviewed by The Information indicates that Anthropic's push to get Claude used inside Office apps has stalled relative to Microsoft's own Copilot. The report lands days before Anthropic's IPO and bears on its enterprise productivity ambitions.

title: OpenAI Explored $5 Billion–Plus Acquisition of Startup That Decodes How AI 'Thinks'
summary: OpenAI previously explored acquiring an AI interpretability startup, which works on decoding how AI models reason internally, for at least $5 billion, according to The Information. The talks highlight the rising strategic value placed on interpretability research among frontier labs.

title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Digital Wallet
summary: OpenAI announced a ChatGPT digital wallet that lets its Dot assistant make online purchases without directly accessing shoppers' card details. The move extends OpenAI's push into agentic commerce.

title: Alibaba Unveils New Flagship AI Model Qwen4-Max
summary: Alibaba added Qwen4-Max as the new flagship of its Qwen family, the world's most downloaded open-weight model series. Alibaba says it beats Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro on coding benchmarks, though unlike most Qwen models it is not open weight.

title: Nokia, Telia Target EU AI Compute Needs
summary: Nokia and Telia lead a Nordic consortium formed to build an AI gigafactory, aiming to win business under a European initiative to create a supercomputing leader. The bid positions Nordic telecom and infrastructure players in the EU's push for sovereign AI compute.

title: Millicom Inks $1.7B Deal for Entel Peru
summary: Millicom signed an agreement to buy Entel Peru for $1.7 billion including lease liabilities. The acquisition would expand the group's footprint to 13 Latin American markets.

title: FCC Tees Up April 2027 for Upper C-Band Auction
summary: The U.S. FCC will open bidding in its upper C-Band spectrum auction on April 27, 2027. Chair Brendan Carr pitched the auction as creating a 5G 'super band' unmatched by other industrialized countries.

title: JPMorgan Chase Software Bug Disrupts Payments Across U.S. Banks
summary: A software bug in JPMorgan Chase's on-premises hardware disrupted transactions for hours on Monday, with payment delays spilling over to Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist whenever Chase was a counterparty. Chase said there was no evidence of a cyberattack and processing returned to normal by early evening; it was the third major U.S. system failure in five days, after a Microsoft 365 outage and a nationwide FAA ground stop.

title: Nvidia Beats Estimates in First Earnings Report After Jensen Huang's Ouster
summary: Nvidia topped Wall Street expectations in its first quarterly report since founding CEO Jensen Huang was pushed out. Interim CEO Colette Kress was expected to face extensive investor questions about leadership, export-control exposure and the company's direction.

title: Anthropic Plans to Raise IPO Price After Strong Demand
summary: Anthropic intends to lift the price range of its initial public offering after strong investor demand during its roadshow. The pitch held up despite market turbulence and the shock resignation of Nvidia's Jensen Huang, ahead of the company's planned public debut this week.

title: Alice Huang's Husband Built a Data-Center Empire Backed by the Chinese State
summary: The WSJ reports that Kang Wei, husband of Alice Huang, built a data-center business with backing from the Chinese state while his wife was involved with Nvidia's then-CEO Jensen Huang. The report adds to the scrutiny of Nvidia's China ties that preceded Huang's resignation.

title: OpenAI Partners With NATO On Cyber Defenses
summary: OpenAI is making its advanced cybersecurity models available to NATO, whose technology and cyber hub of more than 3,000 civilian and military experts is using them to probe suspicious activity, find vulnerabilities and deploy fixes. The deal extends OpenAI's push into government and security work.

title: Genesis AI, a Robotics Startup, Raises $500 Million
summary: Robotics startup Genesis AI has raised $500 million to pursue what CEO Zhou Xian describes as the world's best general-purpose robot. The round is one of the larger recent bets on AI-driven robotics.

title: Nvidia Forms National-Security Committee After Huang's Exit
summary: Nvidia is creating a board committee to oversee national-security policy, export-control compliance and global trade risks following Jensen Huang's departure. The move responds to allegations about chip smuggling into China and mounting government scrutiny of the company.

title: Lush's CEO Says He Learned His Leadership Values in Grade School
summary: Lush co-founder and CEO Mark Constantine discussed a new parental-leave policy for North American full-time staff and the fallout from the retailer's Gaza awareness campaign, which ended its relationship with landlord Westfield Australia and will require relocating 10 mall stores as leases expire. The private company reported 9.2% brand sales growth for fiscal 2025 while facing cocoa-cost and tariff pressures.

title: Nvidia Directors Should Explain
summary: Martin Peers argues Nvidia's board must explain why it pushed Jensen Huang to resign, after reversing its earlier stated confidence in him, or face a growing reinstatement campaign backed by investors and even President Trump. Shareholders owning 15% for a year could call a special meeting, though that bar is hard to reach; Nvidia shares fell another 4% Monday to $156.14, down 35% since early October.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: Commerce Department Restricts Chinese AI Firms' Remote Access to U.S. Chips
summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security issued a long-awaited rule barring Chinese AI companies from using overseas data centres, mainly in Southeast Asia, to access export-controlled chips. Shares of Chinese AI firms MiniMax and Z.ai fell on fears of tighter chip access after Jensen Huang's resignation.

title: Blackstone Data-Center REIT Buys Stakes in AWS Joint Ventures
summary: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust is acquiring 75% stakes in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services, valuing the deal at about $5 billion. It launches the REIT's strategy of buying data centres with long-term leases to major cloud providers.

title: How Google's New AI Chip Software Helps It Battle Nvidia
summary: Google's open-source TorchTPU lets developers run existing PyTorch workloads on its TPUs with minimal code changes, aiming to erode the lock-in of Nvidia's CUDA software. Paired with Nvidia's leadership turmoil, cloud firms report growing interest in AMD and Google chips; Morgan Stanley forecasts TPU hardware sales could top $81 billion next year, though one cloud-spending tracker counts only 16 of about 5,000 clients using TPUs at scale.

title: How JPMorgan, Citi Missed Megaspeed Risks in a $2.8 Billion Data Center Loan
summary: JPMorgan and Citigroup lent in 2025 to a Southeast Asian data-center operator that did business with Megaspeed, a company at the centre of the Nvidia and Jensen Huang scandal. The case highlights banks' indirect exposure to problematic firms through borrowers and raises questions about due diligence on complex ownership structures in the region.

title: OpenAI's Astra Is a Boon to Robotics, Says Nvidia Robotics Chief Deepu Talla
summary: Nvidia robotics head Deepu Talla called OpenAI's Astra model, released in September, a breakthrough for general-purpose robots because of its grasp of the physical world. He said it has made some kinds of robot-training data 100 times faster to create and could help automate deploying robots in factories.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: The $31-Billion Quebecor Bid That Would Reshape Telecom
summary: Quebecor has made an unsolicited, non-binding proposal to acquire Telus for about $31 billion, offering $6.35 in cash plus 0.17 Quebecor shares per Telus share, roughly a 60% premium. A deal would cut Canada's big telecom carriers from four to three and test competition law, needing approval from several agencies and Industry Minister Mélanie Joly; Telus has formed a special committee to review it.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: The Risky Business of Data Centres in Alberta
summary: Alberta's push to attract AI data centres, including Meta's $13-billion project, has drawn more than 145 announced facilities, over 75% of Canada's total, as the province targets $100 billion of investment in five years. Globe reporting finds growing rural dissent over rushed consultations and land deals, which could prove politically costly for Premier Danielle Smith after data centres hurt Republicans in U.S. midterms.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Canaccord CEO Launches $1.6-Billion Take-Private Bid
summary: Canaccord Genuity CEO Dan Daviau has launched a $1.6-billion bid at $15.27 a share to take the investment dealer private. It is the second time the firm's leadership team has attempted a management buyout.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: TC Energy Expects 25% Rise in NGTL Pipeline Demand
summary: TC Energy says it will soon finalize its NOVA Gas Transmission annual plan, which projects total demand on the system to rise 25% over the next five years. The outlook reflects rising Western Canadian gas needs, including from proposed data centres.

title: Vulcan Rocket Failure Destroys 40 Amazon Leo Satellites
summary: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes into flight, destroying all 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites aboard in the first total mission failure in ULA's 20-year history. Amazon has about 400 Leo satellites in orbit against a need for more than 3,200, and the setback widens Starlink's lead.

title: Hyperscale Data Centers Rival Denmark's Emissions
summary: Harvard research on 403 U.S. hyperscale data centres estimates they used 82 TWh of electricity from May 2024 to April 2025, about 1.8% of U.S. demand, and emitted roughly 25.7 million metric tons of CO2, comparable to Denmark. About 54% of their power came from fossil fuels, and Virginia, Oregon, Ohio and Iowa accounted for over half of consumption.

title: Nvidia Highlights 3 Early AI-RAN Use Cases
summary: Nvidia's VP for AI and telecoms, Soma Velayutham, outlined three credible AI-RAN use cases and admitted the sudden rise of integrated sensing and communications had surprised the company. Separately, T-Mobile US said it will soon run AI-RAN and sensing trials on its road to 6G.

title: Orange Commits Additional €250M to VC Fund
summary: Orange allocated €250 million in fresh capital to its venture fund to back companies in sectors core to its strategic plan. The move expands the operator's investment in startups aligned with its growth priorities.
